name: stable_green.py
mathematical_scope: Numerical product-of-sums control. With positive diag/off and delta=diag-2off>0, each tridiagonal inverse has 1-norm at most 1/delta; permutations and unimodular gauges preserve it, yielding budget (q/delta)^t and error floor max(0,1-budget/sqrt(n)).
input_and_guard_coverage: Only n>=4 and delta>0 are asserted. No nonnegative integer q,t, positive diag or nonnegative off guard. For off<0, delta uses the wrong absolute-value margin; e.g. diag=1,off=-1 yields reported delta=3 although interior absolute margin is -1.
costs: qt dense inverses plus t matrix products and spectral norm: O((qt+t+1)n³) time/O(n²) working storage. The bound itself is scalar arithmetic.
test_evidence: Three default-size tests call example twice each and check strict greater-than; no invalid sign, q/t edge, exact equality or optimized-Python coverage.
acceptance_boundary: Bound accepted only under corrected absolute diagonal-dominance assumptions and valid q/t. Default controls support no new FFT complexity result.
findings: L16–17 missing magnitude/sign contract is a real public-API gap. L37–38 assertions can vanish under optimization.
